# Whole-cap section profiles and the equal-area triangle-endpoint theorem

The section functional below retains the complete supremal convolution
of actual section roots. It is not a replacement of integer sums by an
integral. The integral computes ordinary volume INSIDE the middle fiber.
The triangle theorem proved below controls every ambient halfspace: for
equal-area planar triangle endpoint fibers A,B of area v and any middle
K containing(A+B)/2, the single actual point(0,(g_A+g_B)/2) has raw
mixed area depth at least4v/3. Arbitrary convex endpoint bodies and the
full mixed-integer conjecture remain outside this theorem.

## 1. A sharp directional section-profile lower bound

Let d>=2 and let A,K,B be positive-volume convex bodies in R^d with
(A+B)/2 subset K. Write c=(g_A+g_B)/2. The affine change

    (z,x) -> (z,x-c-z(g_B-g_A)/2)

preserves the mixed lattice, fiber measure and ambient halfspaces. It
makes both endpoint centroids zero and sends the actual candidate
(0,c) to (0,0). Work in these coordinates. Fix a unit vector u, and use
the orthogonal coordinates x=s u+w, w in u-perp. Let

    I_A={s:A_s is nonempty}, f_A(s)=|A_s|_(d-1),
    I_B={s:B_s is nonempty}, f_B(s)=|B_s|_(d-1).

The closed projection intervals I_A,I_B are part of the data. A value
f=0 at a nonempty supporting section must not be confused with an empty
section outside its interval. Put

    h(s)=sup_(a in I_A,b in I_B,a+b=2s)
       [(f_A(a)^(1/(d-1))+f_B(b)^(1/(d-1)))/2]^(d-1),    (1)

using h(s)=0 when the allocation set is empty. Then every actual cap

    H_alpha={(z,x):u.x+alpha z>=0}

has mass at least

    mu(H_alpha) >= J_u(alpha)
      := integral_0^infinity h(s) ds
           +integral_alpha^infinity f_A(s) ds
           +integral_(-alpha)^infinity f_B(s) ds.         (2)

Indeed (A_a+B_b)/2 is contained in the actual middle section K_s for
each allowed allocation in (1). Brunn--Minkowski in u-perp gives its
displayed section-volume lower bound, including nonempty sections of
zero (d-1)-volume. Taking the supremum and integrating s>=0 proves
the first contribution in (2). The other two integrals are EXACT
endpoint cap volumes, since the thresholds of H_alpha at bases -1,+1
are alpha,-alpha. Thus all three terms concern one and the same cap.

All functions are measurable and finite. More explicitly, ordinary
section-root concavity makes the two roots continuous on their closed
projection intervals, with their actual endpoint values. The restricted
allocation sets in (1) are compact, so their suprema are attained.
The supremal convolution of these two concave roots is concave on
(I_A+I_B)/2: combine maximizing allocations at two parameters and use
concavity in each endpoint. In particular h is measurable. Fubini
applies on the bounded intervals. Nonvertical boundaries have zero
d-volume; the argument has retained the closed supporting sections.

This functional lower bound is sharp for these section data. Replace
each A_s and B_s by a centered Euclidean (d-1)-ball of the SAME volume,
with centers on the common u-axis. Section-root concavity proves that
the two resulting bodies A^o,B^o are convex. Their volumes and their
u-coordinate means are unchanged; their transverse means are zero.
For a fixed midpoint section, all Minkowski averages of the balls are
concentric balls. Their union has radius equal to the largest allowed
average radius. Consequently the actual section volume of
M^o=(A^o+B^o)/2 is exactly h(s). Taking K^o=M^o makes (2) equality for
every alpha simultaneously. This is a directional comparison, not an
assertion that this body replacement preserves other halfspace cuts.

If |A|=|B|=v, both section profiles have integral v and first moment
zero. A proof that inf_alpha J_u(alpha)>=3Gamma_d v for every such
profile and every u would be a sufficient new functional input. No such
general inequality is asserted here.

## 2. An explicit area-one family of nonhomothetic triangles

In R_s times R_y define, for w>0,

    T_w=conv{(-w/3,-1/w),(-w/3,1/w),(2w/3,0)}.

Each has area1 and actual centroid0. Its vertical section length is

    f_w(s)=2(2w/3-s)/w^2,  -w/3<=s<=2w/3.              (3)

Take A=T_1, B=T_R with R>=1, and K any body containing M=(A+B)/2.
Unless R=1 the endpoint triangles are not homothetic: their axial
widths have ratio R and their transverse widths have ratio 1/R.
Their sections are centered intervals, so equality holds in (1) for
the actual midpoint M. In the positive s direction its section profile
is obtained by spending available axial displacement first in the
flatter B profile. Thus, with

    l=-(R+1)/6, h=(2R-1)/6, r=(R+1)/3,

the midpoint profile starts at height1+1/R at l, decreases with slope
-2/R^2 to height1 at h, and then decreases with slope-2 to zero at r.
In particular

    |M|=(R+1)/2,
    Q_+(R):=|M intersect {s>=0}|
      =(R+1)/2-(R+1)^2(6R-1)/(36R^2).                   (4)

Here 0 lies in the first segment since h>=0. Formula (4) follows by
subtracting the trapezoid from l to0 from the total area. This computes
the whole forced middle contribution, not only midpoint centroid caps.

## 3. Exact optimal endpoint payment in the positive direction

For H_alpha={s+alpha z>=0}, when both endpoint cuts are proper their
combined area is

    (2/3-alpha)^2+(2R/3+alpha)^2/R^2.

Its minimum occurs at

    alpha_*=2R(R-1)/[3(R^2+1)],
    P_+(R)=4(R+1)^2/[9(R^2+1)].                         (5)

The stationary cut is indeed proper: 0<=alpha_*<2/3 and
alpha_*<=R/3, the latter equivalent to
2(R-1)<=R^2+1. A fully captured endpoint gives area at least1, larger
than P_+(R)<=8/9. If an endpoint is empty, moving its threshold toward
its support endpoint decreases the other captured area until a proper
cut or full-cap transition is reached. Thus no empty-endpoint status
beats the minimum already found. Both empty is impossible because
the two thresholds sum to0 while both upper support values are positive.
These arguments include tangent transitions and prove that (5) is the
exact infimum over all finite alpha, not merely a stationary value.

Combining (4)-(5), every positive-s-direction cap through (0,0) has
mass at least4/3, with exact excess in the minimal middle body

    Q_+(R)+P_+(R)-4/3
      =(R-1)(12R^4-13R^3+27R^2+3R-1)
                      /[36R^2(R^2+1)] >=0.             (6)

The last polynomial, on setting R=1+x, becomes
12x^4+35x^3+60x^2+66x+28, so (6) is proved for every R>=1. Equality
occurs exactly at R=1 in this direction.

## 4. The reverse direction, including its supporting transition

The own reverse cap is

    Q_-(R)=|M|-Q_+(R)=(R+1)^2(6R-1)/(36R^2).

For the reversed endpoint profiles the proper cap sum is concave in
the integer tilt, so a minimum occurs at a support transition or the
full/empty plateau. Making the narrow A cap empty at its upper support
in the reversed direction leaves the B cap with area

    P_-(R)=1-(2R-1)^2/(9R^2).                           (7)

The opposite empty transition has area 1-(2-R)^2/9 for 1<=R<=2 and
area1 for R>=2. It is no smaller than (7): in the first range this is
equivalent to (2-R)<=2-1/R, or R>=1/R. Any full endpoint has area at
least1. Both empty is again impossible. Hence (7) is the exact global
reverse-direction endpoint infimum.

The whole reverse cap therefore has the exact strict excess

    Q_-(R)+P_-(R)-4/3
      =(3R-1)(2R^2-5R+5)/(36R^2)>0, R>=1.             (8)

The quadratic has negative discriminant and positive leading
coefficient. Thus all positive and negative axial continuous normals,
with arbitrary coupled integer tilt and every full/empty status, pay
3Gamma_2=4/3. Pure integer through-middle caps capture at least |K|+1
>=2, so they also pay this amount. Other continuous directions are handled by the complete tent-profile
proof in Sections5--12.

## 5. The exact finite tent-profile system

Every projection profile of an area-one triangle is a tent with width
w>0, peak at fraction theta in [0,1] of its support, peak height2/w,
and support endpoints -(1+theta)w/3 and (2-theta)w/3 after centering
its first moment. Thus general triangle projections have two shape
parameters per endpoint, reduced to a width ratio and two theta values
by common scaling. Their supremal convolution is piecewise affine, and
their endpoint cap sum is piecewise quadratic in the integer tilt.

Here is the exact finite system, including every boundary parameter.
Set w_A=1,w_B=R. Interchanging the two endpoints, if necessary, permits
R>=1 without changing the infimum over integer tilts. For (w,theta) put

    a=-(1+theta)w/3,
    b=(2theta-1)w/3,
    c=(2-theta)w/3.

Its upper-tail area function is

    F_(w,theta)(s)=1,                          s<=a;
        1-(s-a)^2/(theta w^2),                 a<=s<=b;
        (c-s)^2/((1-theta)w^2),                b<=s<=c;
        0,                                    s>=c.       (9)

When theta=0 omit the empty first proper interval; when theta=1 omit
the empty second one. The remaining formulas agree at every common
endpoint. Define the explicit area-one profile body

    E_(w,theta)=conv{(a,0),(b,1/w),(c,0),(b,-1/w)}.

It is a triangle at theta=0,1 and otherwise a kite. Its section
lengths are precisely the triangle tent, and its centroid is zero.
For arbitrary p,q in [0,1], let

    N_(R,p,q)=(E_(1,p)+E_(R,q))/2,
    J_(R,p,q)(alpha)=|N_(R,p,q) intersect {s>=0}|
                         +F_(1,p)(alpha)+F_(R,q)(-alpha). (10)

Equation (10) is exactly the sharp profile lower bound (2), not an
additional relaxation. The polygon N is the convex hull of the at most
16 pairwise vertex midpoints. In particular its first term has an exact
finite polygonal computation for every rational parameter triple.

The full tilt infimum in (10) also has a finite exact computation. Its
breakpoints are the six values

    a_A,b_A,c_A,-a_B,-b_B,-c_B,

with repetitions removed. Outside their range the endpoint sum is1.
On each intervening interval it is a quadratic polynomial. Check the
interval endpoints and also its stationary point when the quadratic
coefficient is positive and that point lies in the interval. A linear
or concave quadratic has no smaller interior value. Thus this list
includes every tilt, every proper-state pairing, every supporting
transition and the full/empty plateau. If the parameters are rational,
all tested tilts and all values are rational. No search over a dense
set of normals is substituted for this directional statement.

The scalar inequality needed is that (10) is at least4/3 for all
R>=1,p,q in[0,1] and all real alpha. Sections2--4 establish the slices
p=q=0 and p=q=1; Sections6--12 prove all remaining parameter cells.

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/screen_supremal_triangle_profiles_three_cap_credit_two_sided.py`
performed a numerical falsification screen over that finite-parameter
family, minimizing each tilt exactly within its numerical quadratic
cells. Its smallest observed whole-profile value was4/3 at identical
one-sided tents. This is only a screen. It is not a proof for all tent
parameters, all triangle directions, all planar bodies, or all d.
The proof that follows uses exact inequalities and polynomial identities;
the numerical screen is not a premise of any result.

## 6. Six exact rational cells for the forced middle cap

This section is an algebraic reduction, valid for all tent parameters.
Write a=1-p, b=1-q and

    S=[1+R+a+Rb]/3,
    H=[2p-1+R(2q-1)]/6.

The right support of N is S/2 and its peak is H. Its four nonconstant
roof segments have lengths p/2,Rq/2,Rb/2,a/2 and height increments
1,1/R,-1/R,-1, in the order determined by concavity. The increasing
segments are sorted by their decreasing positive slopes 2/p and
2/(R^2 q); the decreasing segments are sorted by their increasing
absolute slopes 2/a and 2/(R^2 b). Zero-length segments are omitted.
For R>=1 the following are the only three orders:

* If p<=R^2 q and a<=R^2 b, the order is A-rise,B-rise,B-fall,A-fall,
  and m=|N|=(R+1)/2.
* If p>R^2 q, the order is B-rise,A-rise,B-fall,A-fall,
  and m=[1+p/R+Rb]/2.
* If a>R^2 b, the order is A-rise,B-rise,A-fall,B-fall,
  and m=[1+Rq+a/R]/2.

Both exceptional inequalities cannot hold, since their sum would give
1>R^2. The area formulas follow by summing the four trapezoids.

The cut at zero is always between the end of the first roof segment
and the beginning of the last roof segment. For an initial A-rise its
endpoint is [2p-1-R(1+q)]/6<=0. For an initial B-rise, q<=p/R^2,
and its endpoint is at most [2p/R-R-1-p]/6<0 (at R=1 a harmless
support equality can occur). For a final A-fall its initial point is
[R(2-q)+2p-1]/6>=0. For a final B-fall, q>=1-a/R^2, and its initial
point is at least [R+2-2/R+p(2/R-1)]/6>0. These inequalities follow
directly by minimizing or maximizing the displayed affine expressions
in p in [0,1]. Thus only the TWO middle segments can contain zero.

In particular, when H<=0, the exact own cap Q(R,p,q) is

    Q=S/2-a/4+(S-a)^2/(4R^2 b),       if a<=R^2 b;       (11)
    Q=S/(2R)-b/4+(S-Rb)^2/(4a),      if a>=R^2 b.       (12)

To see (11), the final A segment has length a/2 and height1; the
preceding B segment, from zero to the start of that last segment,
has length (S-a)/2 and slope -2/(R^2 b). Its trapezoid area plus
the last triangle is exactly (11). Equation (12) is the same computation
with last height1/R and last length Rb/2. The subtraction there is
b/4, not Rb/4. When H>=0 use the exact reflection identity

    Q(R,p,q)=m-Q(R,1-p,1-q).                             (13)

Equations (11)-(13), together with the three roof orders, are six
rational cells. At a zero denominator the corresponding segment is
absent and the formula is read by its continuous limit, or computed
directly by the polygon formula (10). No singular division is required.

## 7. A coupled certificate when both optimal tails decrease

Here is one complete branch of the outstanding all-tent problem. Suppose
the ratio of endpoint widths is between 1/5 and5, and a tilt has
both thresholds in their decreasing tent branches.
Then the whole cap lower bound is at least4/3. This includes every
closed limiting configuration of such tilts.

For the proof first assume both thresholds lie in the open branches.
They sum to zero and are at least the two mode coordinates, hence the
sum of mode coordinates is nonpositive: H<=0. Relabel the two tents,
rescaling the axial and transverse coordinates inversely to keep areas1,
so that the last decreasing roof component is the first tent. Its width
is1; let the other width be R, now allowed in [1/5,5]. Write the first
fall parameter a>0 and the second fall parameter b>0, and put

    t=R^2 b/a>=1,    S=[R+1+a(1+t/R)]/3.

The sum of the distances of the two thresholds from their upper supports
is S. Minimizing their sum of squared distances divided by a and at
over all real allocations gives S^2/[a(1+t)]. At an interior minimizing
tilt this is the exact endpoint sum; it is also a lower bound at any
tilt in the two decreasing branches. Equation (11) remains valid after this relabeling. Indeed, if R<1,
a<=R^2 b implies S-a>=0: for R<=1/2 this is immediate from
S-a>=[R+1+a(1/R-2)]/3 with b>=a/R^2; for 1/2<=R<=1
its lower bound is [1+2R-2R^2]/3>0. Thus zero still lies before
the last descending segment. Equation (11) gives

    J >= S/2-a/4+(S-a)^2/(4at)+S^2/[a(1+t)]
       = A a+B+C/a,                                    (14)

where

 C=(R+1)^2(5t+1)/[36t(t+1)],
 A=[-3R^2t^2+5R^2t+4R^2+6Rt^3+10Rt^2-4Rt
       +5t^3+t^2]/[36R^2t(t+1)],
 B=(R+1)[3Rt^2+5Rt-2R+5t^2+t]/[18Rt(t+1)].

We now verify (14)>=4/3 without any omitted feasibility condition.
Set x=R-1 in [-4/5,4] and y=t-1>=0. The numerator of A, expressed
as a polynomial in y, is

 (6x+11)y^3+(-3x^2+22x+41)y^2
     +(-x^2+32x+50)y+6x^2+24x+24.

Every coefficient is positive on this interval. For -1<=x<=0 the
first three are at least5,16,17 respectively; for 0<=x<=4 the
second and third, being concave quadratics, have positive endpoint
minima, and the first is positive. The last is6(x+2)^2. Thus A,C>0.
Direct simplification gives

 4AC-(4/3-B)^2=N(x,y)/[108Rt(t+1)],

 N=(-3x^3+33x^2+8x+52)y^2
       +(-18x^3+86x^2-16x+56)y+96x^2.                 (15)

For -4/5<=x<=0 the first coefficient is at least52-32/5 and the
second at least56. For 0<=x<=4 the first is positive, while the
second is at least14x^2-16x+56>0. Hence N>=0. If B>=4/3,
(14)>4/3 immediately. If B<4/3, (15) and arithmetic-geometric mean
give A a+C/a>=2sqrt(AC)>=4/3-B. This proves the branch claim.

Equality forces x=y=0 in (15), followed by a=1 in
A a+B+C/a=a/3+2/3+1/(3a). It is exactly the identical one-sided
tent configuration. Boundary parameters follow by continuity of the
finite polygon and quadratic-tail formulas. A cap whose minimum occurs
in a mixed increasing/decreasing cell, a supporting transition not
approximable by this branch, or an endpoint-width ratio above5 is not
covered by this argument alone. Those cases are treated separately in Sections8--12.

## 8. Every tilt is paid when the endpoint widths differ by at least9/2

This gives a second complete part of the finite tent problem, independent
of the statuses of the endpoint cuts. Continue with widths1,R, R>=1.
Fix the peak point of the first profile, with coordinate b_A=(2p-1)/3
and section height2. In the midpoint convolution this supplies the lower
roof

    1+f_B(2s-b_A)/2,
       (b_A+a_B)/2<=s<=(b_A+c_B)/2.

Since -b_A is in [a_B,c_B] for R>=1, its contribution above zero is
(c_B+b_A)/2+F_B(-b_A)/4. From the right endpoint of this interval to
the right endpoint of the whole midpoint, fixing the upper support point
of B and using the falling part of A supplies a disjoint triangular
roof piece of area(1-p)/4. This entire second piece lies above zero.
Consequently

    Q >= R(2-q)/6+(p+1)/12+F_B((1-2p)/3)/4
      >= R/6+1/12+F_B(1/3)/4.                         (16)

The second inequality uses p>=0,q<=1 and monotonicity of the tail.
The profile body E_(R,q) has area1 and centroid0, hence F_B(0)>=4/9
(this also follows directly from (9)). Its upper support c_B is at
least R/3. Contract its cap at zero toward any upper support point by
the factor 1-1/(3c_B). Convexity sends that contracted cap into its cap
at1/3. Thus

    F_B(1/3)>=(4/9)(1-1/R)^2.                          (17)

Every integer tilt has one nonpositive endpoint threshold, so its
combined endpoint tails are at least4/9. Equations (16)-(17) give the
fully status-independent whole-cap bound

    J >= R/6+1/12+(1-1/R)^2/9+4/9.                   (18)

The right side increases for R>=1. At R=9/2 it equals
4/3+17/1458. Therefore J>4/3 for every tilt, every p,q, and R>=9/2.
Pure integer caps are already larger than2.

Combining this with Section7 proves J>=4/3 for EVERY width ratio
whenever both endpoint thresholds lie in their decreasing tent branches.
Indeed ratios at most5 are covered there after relabeling; ratios at
least9/2 are covered by (18), with an overlap. The remaining part to prove is therefore the compact width interval
1<=R<=9/2 with mixed increasing/decreasing optimal tails or the
supporting transitions not already included in the decreasing case.

## 9. The increasing tent is no wider than the decreasing tent

This is another complete stationary branch, including its feasible
limits. Label the tent with an increasing density at its endpoint cut
as the first tent, and normalize its width to1. Suppose the other,
decreasing-density tent has width R>=1. Write the first mode parameter
as a, and the second fall parameter as b. At a strict local minimum
of the paired tails, equality of the two section lengths and positivity
of the paired second derivative require

    V=R^2 b=at,  0<=t<1,
    T=1-R+a(1-t/R)>0,
    P=1-T^2/[9a(1-t)].                                 (19)

The distances into the first rising and second falling pieces are
aT/[3a(1-t)] and atT/[3a(1-t)] respectively. These statements follow
also by minimizing
1-x^2/a+(x-T/3)^2/(at) with the appropriate distances; equivalently
use the common section length2T/[3a(1-t)]. Formula (19) itself is
valid at t=0 by continuity, when the second cap is supporting and empty.

Necessarily R<2, since T>0 and a<=1 give R<1+a<=2. Moreover the
stationary thresholds lie in the required branches automatically:

    T-3a(1-t)/R
      =1-R+a[1+(2t-3)/R]
      <=1-R+max(0,1-1/R)<0,                            (20)

for R>1; at R=1 it is -2a(1-t)<0. The other branch condition is
weaker because R>=1. Thus there is no omitted mode-contact boundary
inside this parameter domain.

Put w=a(1+t). The midpoint peak satisfies
6H=2T+3(R-1)>0. Its total area is

    m=(R+1)/2 + dist(w,[1,R^2])/(2R).                  (21)

The reflected positive-cap parameter S_- is R+T/3. Write Q_- for
the midpoint cap below zero. If w<=R^2, equation (11) gives

    Q_-=S_-/2-a/4+(S_--a)^2/[4(R^2-at)].              (22)

If w>=R^2, equation (12) instead gives

    Q_-=S_-/(2R)-(1-at/R^2)/4
                       +[S_--R+at/R]^2/(4a).         (23)

Thus J=m-Q_-+P. For fixed R,t, each term in (22) or (23) is
affine in a except a square of an affine function divided by a positive
affine function. Such a quotient is convex (its second derivative is
2(AD-BC)^2/(Ca+D)^3 for numerator(Aa+B)^2 and denominator Ca+D).
The negative square in (19) is concave. Since (21) is affine within
each of its three cells, J is concave in a on each cell.

Consequently its minimum on every closed feasible cell occurs at a=1,
T=0, or one of the roof-order boundaries w=1,w=R^2. The T=0 limit
has P=1 and Q>=4/9 by ordinary cap BM at the two endpoint centroids,
so is safely above4/3. On w=1 substitute t=(1-a)/a. Then m is
constant, (22) is affine plus a square over R^2-1+a, and (19) is
1 minus a square over9(2a-1). Hence J is AGAIN concave in a on this
boundary. Its feasible a interval starts at T=0 and ends at a=1:
at a=1/2, T=-(2R-1)(R-1)/(2R)<=0. On w=R^2 substitute
t=(R^2-a)/a. Here m is constant, (22) is a square over4a,
and (19) is1 minus a square over9(2a-R^2). It too is concave.
This boundary is feasible only when R<sqrt2; at a=R^2/2 its T is
(R-1)(R-2)/2<=0, and its other endpoint is a=1. These two boundary
reductions therefore leave only a=1 and the already safe T=0 limits.
At R=1,t tending to1, P tends to1 uniformly in a in[0,1], so the
otherwise singular corner also has the same safe limiting bound.

Here is an exact certificate for a=1. Set x=R-1 in[0,1) and
y=1-t in(0,1]. Then T>0 is precisely y>x^2. In the central roof
cell w<=R^2, the numerator of J-4/3 over the positive denominator
36R^2(R^2-t)(1-t) is

 N_1=(-6x-11)y^3+(3x^2+4x+15)y^2
        +(6x^5+33x^4+76x^3+66x^2+30x)y-4x^6-8x^5.

Using y<=1 on the negative cubic term and y>=x^2 on the positive
linear term gives

 N_1 >=(3x^2-2x+4)y^2
             +6x^7+29x^6+68x^5+66x^4+30x^3>0.        (24)

In the other cell w>=R^2, the numerator over36R^2(1-t) is

 N_2=-4y^3-(4x^2+18x+7)y^2
                     +(-x^4+17x^2+30x+15)y-4x^4.

This cell has y<=U:=1-2x-x^2. Write N_2=y B(y)-4x^4. The
quadratic B is decreasing for y>=0, and

    B(U)=-x^4+10x^3+48x^2+42x+4>=4x^2+4

for0<=x<=1. Therefore

    N_2>=4y+4x^2(y-x^2)>0.                            (25)

This proves J>=4/3 throughout the stationary mixed branch with the
increasing tent no wider than the decreasing tent. The proof keeps its
actual centroid normalization and does not replace the two tail areas
by independent minima.

For parameters strictly between0 and1, tail functions are C^1 at their
mode and support transitions. A minimum with both cuts on increasing
pieces is impossible because their sum is strictly concave; full caps
cost at least1 and hence pay with Q>=4/9. Mode contacts with the other
cut decreasing are already covered by Section7. Other mode contacts
cannot minimize the sum, and an empty supporting transition with the
other cut proper has a nonzero derivative. If a mixed quadratic has zero second derivative, it either has no
interior minimum or is constant. In the constant case t=1,T=0 and
P=1, so Q+P>=13/9. Degenerate facet transitions
are retained by continuity of the exact finite formulas. Accordingly,
the branch still to be treated below is the one where the
increasing-density tent is WIDER than the decreasing-density tent,
in the compact ratio range below9/2. Sections10--11 prove that branch.

## 10. The wider-increasing branch when the midpoint peak is nonnegative

Continue the mixed stationary notation, but now 0<R<1: the increasing
tent has width1 and the decreasing tent width R. It is more useful to
use independent variables a,V, where 0<=a<=1, 0<=V<=R^2, and

    D=a-V,  T=1-R+a-V/R,  P=1-T^2/(9D).

The proper stationary branch has D>0,T>0. Its first cut is on its
increasing piece precisely when T<=3D; this also ensures the second
cut is on its decreasing piece because R<1. Write c=1-R. The
midpoint peak is H=(2T-3c)/6. This section assumes H>=0.

Fix R. The closed feasible domain is the polygon

    0<=a<=1,  0<=V<=R^2,
    3c/2<=T<=3(a-V).                                  (26)

In particular D>=c/2>0, so every denominator below is strictly positive.
The value V=0 is interpreted by the continuous supporting-empty limit.
Put w=a+V and S_-=R+T/3. Then

    m=(1+1/R)/2+dist(w,[R^2,1])/(2R).

The reflected cap is given by (22) or (23), with at replaced by V.
Within each of the three cells cut out by w=R^2 and w=1, m is affine
in(a,V), Q_- is affine plus the square of an affine function divided
by a positive affine function, and P is1 minus another such quotient.
Therefore J=m-Q_-+P is JOINTLY concave in(a,V) on each cell.
Its minimum on each compact cell occurs at a vertex. The following
checks cover all such vertices, including vertices on nontrivial edges.

### 10.1 The edge a=1

Here t=V belongs to[0,R^2]. The value of J-4/3 is N_2 from Section9
divided by36R^2(1-t), with x=R-1 and y=1-t. Thus
x in(-1,0), y in[1-R^2,1]. The second derivative of N_2 in y is

    -2[12y+4x^2+18x+7]<0,

because y>=-2x-x^2 gives the bracket at least
-8x^2-6x+7>0 on[-1,0]. Hence the numerator is concave in y,
and it suffices to check its two endpoints. At t=0 it is

    R[-5R^3+20R^2-17R+6]>0:

the bracket is at least15R^2-17R+6>0. At t=R^2 it is

    R(R-1)[R^4-13R^3-26R^2+14R-6]>0,

since the last bracket is at most-25R^2+14R-6<0. This proves the
whole a=1 edge, not merely selected endpoint parameters.

### 10.2 The edge T=3D and the edge H=0

At T=3D the first threshold is exactly at its mode and the second
is on its decreasing piece. Section7 and its limiting cases apply.

On H=0 we have T=3c/2 and

    V=Ra-Rc/2,
    c/2<=a<=(1+R)/2,
    P=1-c/[4(a+R/2)].                                 (27)

If w=a+V>=1, the entire positive roof consists of the B-fall followed
by the A-fall, giving

    Q=V(2R+1)/(4R^2)+(1-a)/4.

If w<=1, the order is reversed and

    Q=(1-a)(R+2)/(4R)+V/(4R^2).

These formulas are affine in a. The value P in (27) is concave in a.
Thus J is concave on each of these at most two intervals. At the lower
endpoint a=c/2,V=0 the first threshold is at its mode, already covered.
At the only possible breakpoint w=1, a=1-R/2; this belongs to the
interval only when R>=1/2. The exact excess there is

    J-4/3=(9R^2-8R+3)/(24R)>0.                         (28)

At the upper endpoint a=(1+R)/2,V=R^2, its excess is

    (18R^2+23R-11)/[24(2R+1)]>0,         R>=1/2;
    (-6R^3+11R^2+R+6)/[24R(2R+1)]>0,    R<=1/2.        (29)

The first numerator increases on[1/2,1] and equals5 at1/2. For the
second use6R^3<=3R^2. This covers every vertex on H=0.

### 10.3 The remaining possible vertices

All original boundary lines of (26) are a=1, V=0, V=R^2,
T=3D, and H=0; a=0 is infeasible because D>=c/2>0.
The first, fourth, and fifth boundaries have just been covered in full.
On V=0 or V=R^2, any endpoint not on those boundaries can only
be the intersection with one of the two internal roof lines. Apart
from already covered a=1 or infeasible a=0, there are exactly two:

    C_0:(a,V)=(R^2,0),          feasible only if R>=1/2;
    C_1:(a,V)=(1-R^2,R^2),     with H>=0 only if R<=1/2.

There is no intersection of the two internal roof lines for0<R<1.
At C_0 the excess is

    -[5R^4-4R^3+12R^2-22R+5]/(36R^2)>0.               (30)

The polynomial in brackets is convex, since its second derivative
60R^2-24R+24 is positive. On[1/2,1] its endpoint values are
-51/16 and-4, both negative, so it is negative throughout.

At C_1 the excess has positive denominator36R(R-1)(2R^2-1)
and numerator

    6R^6+18R^5-29R^4-15R^3+42R^2-26R+6.              (31)

For z=2R in[0,1], this polynomial equals
sum_(j=0)^6 b_j binom(6,j) z^j(1-z)^(6-j), with

    (b_0,...,b_6)=(6,23/6,71/30,241/160,83/80,23/32,15/32).

All coefficients are positive. This is an exact polynomial identity,
not a numerical positivity test.

These exhaust the vertices of every cell. Joint concavity therefore
proves J>=4/3 throughout (26). The last mixed stationary case has the increasing tent wider AND H<0.
Its Hessian has a different sign structure and is handled separately
in Section11.

## 11. The wider-increasing branch with negative midpoint peak

Continue with 0<R<1, c=1-R, D=a-V and T=c+a-V/R. If H<=0,
the paired stationarity conditions are T<=3D and T<=3c/2.
The full feasible domain at fixed R is exactly the triangle with vertices

    E=(c/2,0),
    F=((1+R)/2,R^2),
    G=((1-2R+3R^2)/2,R^2).                            (32)

Indeed 0<=V<=R^2 and the two remaining inequalities are precisely

    c/2+V(3R-1)/(2R) <= a <= c/2+V/R.

The interval lengths are3Vc/(2R)>=0. Every point of this triangle
has 0<a<1, D>=c^2/2>0 and T>0, as is checked at its three vertices
and then by affinity. There are no missing T=0 or D=0 edges.

When R>=7/9, the mode constraint gives

    P=1-T^2/(9D)>=1-T/3>=1-c/2=(1+R)/2.

Since Q>=4/9, this already gives J>=4/3, including R=7/9.
When R<=2/9, Section8 applies after interchanging widths, including
R=2/9. It remains to treat the compact range2/9<=R<=7/9.

### 11.1 Reduction to three edges and one roof line

Set L=1-a and S=1-T/3. For w=a+V>=1 the positive cap is

    Q=S/2-L/4+(S-L)^2/(4V),                            (33)

and for w<=1 it is

    Q=S/(2R)-V/(4R^2)+(S-V/R)^2/(4L).                 (34)

Thus J on either cell is affine plus ONE positive quadratic perspective
minus the convex perspective T^2/(9D). We do not claim joint concavity.
Instead fix an interior point of either cell. Write its positive term
as l(a,V)^2/m(a,V), absorbing positive constants into l or m. Both
l and m are affine and m>0. There is a nonzero direction e in R^2
satisfying

    directional_derivative_e l
       =(l(a,V)/m(a,V)) directional_derivative_e m.

This is one homogeneous linear equation in two unknowns, so such e
always exists, including when that equation is identically zero. Along
the resulting line through the point, l/m is constant wherever m>0;
the positive perspective is therefore affine. The negative perspective
is concave along that line. Extend the line to its maximal segment in
the same compact polygonal cell. Its endpoints are on the cell boundary,
all denominators stay positive, and concavity on the segment gives J
at least the smaller of its endpoint values. Here L>0 throughout the
triangle; on the cell w>=1, V>0 throughout its closure. Also D>=c^2/2.
Thus a lower bound on the cell boundaries proves it throughout.

The edges EF (H=0) and EG (the first cut at its mode) were proved in
Sections10 and7, respectively. The only new boundaries are FG,
where V=R^2, and the internal segment w=1. They are checked next by
exact rational polynomial certificates.

### 11.2 The full-fall edge V=R^2

Parametrize this entire edge by0<=u<=1:

    a=(1-2R+3R^2)/2+3R(1-R)u/2.

Substituting (33) into J-4/3 gives A(R,u)/[24(3Ru-R+1)], where

 A=18R^3u^3-39R^3u^2+18R^3u+3R^3
       -36R^2u^3+51R^2u^2+36R^2u-33R^2
       +18Ru^3-18Ru^2-24Ru+47R+6u^2-17.              (35)

This is used only when w>=1, equivalently

    u>=U(R):=(1+2R-5R^2)/[3R(1-R)].

The function U is strictly decreasing, since
U'=-(3R^2-2R+1)/[3R^2(1-R)^2]<0. Such points require R>=1/2.
They are covered by these THREE rational rectangles:

    [1/2,3/5] times [5/9,1],
    [3/5,5/8] times [19/45,1],
    [5/8,7/9] times [0,1].                            (36)

Here U(3/5)=5/9 and U(5/8)=19/45. On each rectangle A has strictly
positive tensor Bernstein coefficients, listed in Appendix A below.
The minima of those coefficient lists are8/81,863692/421875,111/512.

Substitution of (34), used when w<=1, instead gives
B(R,u)/[24R(3R+1-3Ru)(3Ru-R+1)], where

 B=-45R^5u^3+129R^5u^2-123R^5u+39R^5
       -9R^4u^3-48R^4u^2+135R^4u-78R^4
       +54R^3u^3-9R^3u^2-111R^3u+60R^3
       -54R^2u^2+81R^2u-28R^2-6Ru+R+6.              (37)

All displayed denominators are positive. This cell has u<=U(R),
so no such point has R>=7/10 because U(7/10)<0. Its feasible points
are covered by

    [2/9,1/2] times [0,1],
    [1/2,3/5] times [0,1],
    [3/5,7/10] times [0,5/9].                         (38)

The three exact tensor Bernstein coefficient tables for B also appear
in Appendix A. Their minima are5/2,168/125,138693/100000.
This proves the whole FG edge with both roof orders retained.

### 11.3 The internal equal-slope segment w=1

This segment can meet (32) only for R>=1/2. Put D=2a-1>0. Then

    Q=(1-T/3)^2/[2(1-D)],
    T=[(1-R)(2R-1)+(R+1)D]/(2R).

Its mode constraint and H<=0 give

    (1-R)(2R-1)/(5R-1)<=D<=1-R.

Enlarge the allowed set by discarding the additional condition V<=R^2.
Write

    D=(1-R)[s_0+(1-s_0)v],
    s_0=(2R-1)/(5R-1),  0<=v<=1.                     (39)

We use this enlargement only where D>0. Direct algebra gives J-4/3
equal to N/[36(1-a)(2a-1)], where

    N=(6a-5)T^2-6(2a-1)T+24a^2-18a+3
      =3(1-R) C(R,v)/[4(5R-1)^3],                    (40)

and

 C=27R^5v^3+234R^5v^2+576R^5v+288R^5
       -483R^4v^2-984R^4v-208R^4
       -54R^3v^3+276R^3v^2+1080R^3v-192R^3
       +54R^2v^2-648R^2v+240R^2
       +27Rv^3-78Rv^2+168Rv-64R-3v^2.               (41)

For R in[1/2,7/9], v in[0,1], its tensor Bernstein coefficient
matrix of degrees(5,3), after R=1/2+(5/18)x, is

    [0,             9/2,            27/8,           135/32]
    [1,            35/6,            85/16,             27/4]
    [2,           139/18,           913/108,           391/36]
    [2362/729,   7874/729,         20051/1458,       12961/729]
    [36544/6561,108224/6561,       152048/6561,      197392/6561]
    [71680/6561,547456/19683,      805792/19683,     351520/6561].

All entries are nonnegative, so N>=0. This proves the internal segment.
The infeasible singular corner R=1/2,v=0,D=0 was never divided by;
its inclusion in the polynomial rectangle does not enlarge the actual
positive-denominator domain.

The constant-ratio line reduction and these edge certificates complete
the negative-peak mixed stationary branch. The proofs of Sections7--11
together cover every finite tilt of every pair of triangle tent profiles,
with the complete finite-status synthesis given next.

## 12. The all-tent theorem and the actual-center consequence

The bounded theorem synthesized here is about planar triangle endpoint
fibers, not arbitrary convex endpoint bodies and not the full mixed-integer
conjecture. The preceding finite branch certificates establish the following
scalar assertion:

    For all R>0, p,q in[0,1], and alpha real,
       J_(R,p,q)(alpha)>=4/3.                         (42)

Here is the complete finite-status argument. First suppose0<p,q<1.
The endpoint-tail sum is continuous, piecewise quadratic, and equals1
outside a bounded interval. Thus a minimum is attained. A full endpoint
costs at least1, and the middle contribution is at least4/9: the two
endpoint centroid caps each have area at least4/9, and their midpoint
lies in the middle cap, whose area is bounded below by ordinary planar
Brunn--Minkowski. Such a tilt is already safe. Two increasing pieces
have a strictly concave quadratic sum and cannot contain an interior
minimum. Two decreasing pieces, including mode contacts, are covered
by Sections7--8. A mixed interior minimum with positive second derivative
has exactly the stationary parameters(19). If its increasing tent is
no wider, Section9 applies; if it is wider, Sections10--11 apply according
to the sign of H. When the mixed second derivative is zero, an interior
minimum requires a constant polynomial; this has T=0 and paired mass1.
A negative second derivative has no interior minimum.

The two tails are C^1 at every mode and supporting transition for
0<p,q<1. At a mode with the other threshold strictly on an increasing
piece, a zero derivative is followed on one side by a strictly concave
quadratic and cannot be a minimum. A mode contact with the other threshold
on its decreasing piece belongs to Section7, including simultaneous mode
contacts. At an empty supporting transition the derivative is nonzero if
the other cut is proper, so it cannot minimize; if both cuts are at
nonproper transitions, their total is at least1. Both endpoints cannot
be empty because their two positive upper supports have positive sum,
whereas the thresholds sum to zero. Lower-support contacts include a
full cap and were already handled. This exhausts the finite menu.

For p or q in{0,1}, approximate those parameters by interior values,
keeping R and the tested alpha fixed. The polygon vertices in(10) vary
continuously; their convex hulls and their positive-halfplane intersection
areas converge. This can also be read directly from the finite piecewise
formulas(9)--(13). Endpoint tail areas converge for every threshold,
including a supporting threshold, because these are two-dimensional
areas and supporting lines have zero area. Thus(42) passes pointwise
to every boundary parameter. No exchange of an infimum with a limit is
required. Interchanging the endpoints and reversing alpha reduces R<1
to R>=1; the separate mixed-branch relabeling in Sections9--11 is also
measure preserving. The seams R=9/2 in Section8 and the reciprocal
R=2/9 in Section11 are included, as is R=7/9 in its elementary bound.
H=0 is covered explicitly by Section10 and all formulas agree there.

Consequently let A,B be arbitrary positive-area planar triangles of
common area v, and let K be any planar convex body containing(A+B)/2.
For the actual three-fiber set

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B),

put y=(0,(g_A+g_B)/2). This is one deterministic point of S: its
continuous coordinate belongs to(A+B)/2 subset K. Then every closed
ambient halfspace containing y has raw mixed area at least4v/3.

To prove this consequence, apply the single global shear in Section1,
which sends the two endpoint centroids and y to zero and preserves all
fiber areas and ambient halfspaces. For any continuous normal u not zero,
normalize it to unit length. The two actual directional triangle profiles
are tents with integral v and first moment zero. A common area scaling
reduces v to1; inverse scalings of the axial and transverse coordinates
then make the first width1 without changing area. These changes only
normalize this directional calculation and leave the tested point at zero.
Section1 and(42) give the asserted4v/3 bound for every integer tilt.
Thus oblique normals, not only vertical cylinders, are controlled.
For a pure integer through-y normal, the closed halfspace captures all
of K and one endpoint. Since |K|>=|(A+B)/2|>=v, its mass is at least2v.
A containing halfspace whose boundary does not pass through y contains
the parallel halfspace whose boundary does, so the same lower bound holds.

Writing k=|K|, a separate valid middle candidate g_K gives raw depth
at least(4/9)k by its own fiber. Thus

    max_(z,x in S) raw_depth_S(z,x)
         >=max(4v/3,4k/9).                             (43)

In particular the stronger edge credit requested for1<=k/v<=3,
namely raw depth >=(k+v)/3, follows at the single point y above.
The same bound for k>=3v follows from g_K. Normalizing(43) by k+2v
also gives the uniform bound4/15 for this triangle-endpoint subclass.
No arbitrary-body localization to tents has been used or asserted.

The constant4v/3 for the specified point is attained when A=B=K is
a triangle: its centroid is the chosen point, and a canonical simplex
cap through it has area4v/9 in each of the three fibers. This verifies
the scale of the proved whole-cap profile bound, not a sharpness claim
for the derived normalized4/15 bound.

# Whole-cap section profiles and the equal-area triangle-endpoint theorem

The section functional below retains the complete supremal convolution
of actual section roots. It is not a replacement of integer sums by an
integral. The integral computes ordinary volume INSIDE the middle fiber.

equal-area planar triangle endpoint fibers A,B of area v and any middle
K containing(A+B)/2, the single actual point(0,(g_A+g_B)/2) has raw
mixed area depth at least4v/3. Arbitrary convex endpoint bodies and the
full mixed-integer conjecture remain outside this theorem.
